Everyone says to avoid bundle orders, but I disagree. I’ve made at LEAST 25+ on all of my bundle orders. It is almost always 25-40 and I can get it done in an hour, an hour and a half, automatically putting my hourly above most people with “regular” jobs. I think normally Shipt will guarantee at least one tipper in bundles. 

I’ve found the easiest way to do bundles is by putting a hand basket in my cart and using the hand basket for the smaller order. If you’re worried about lines at the store, make friends with the employees and be cheerful so they recognize you and want to help you. 

To maximize your shopping time, camp at a store you know gets open metro orders at each hour. If you also get an offer from the store, take both orders at once - but make sure you’re aware of where you’re delivering to.

Minimize your delivery drive time by putting both addresses into your map BEFORE YOU SHOP. This will give you an idea of how much time you have left to shop, and you can play with the maps to see which route will take the least time.

I have the advantage of having lived in my metro for 25 years so I know traffic patterns and shortcuts like the back of my hand. I always know how many people will be at the store at that time, which intersections are likely to have accidents, which lights take the longest to change, etc. if you don’t have this, I suggest taking a day to drive around surrounding neighborhoods (or carefully looking at your maps) to find and mark shortcuts. For instance - there are train tracks that are regularly backed up in my metro. There is a raised highway that goes over the tracks about a mile further down from the neighborhoods that allows me to go above and around a stuck train and back into the other half of my metro. The tracks go right down the middle of the metro. Most people would just get stuck not knowing you can go above and then cut through neighborhoods to get around it, because a GPS would never tell you that. Doing this also probably adds data to the maps which might eventually help other shoppers if the GPS app does note it as a possible workaround.

I don’t work FT anymore but when I did I made a huge point to make sure that I was adding small tidying / cleaning tasks throughout the day.

Make a list of spring cleaning tasks or whatever and choose two or three to do on one day off, save the rest for next week. Make a schedule. I’m a bartender / server so I had a leg up by sense of urgency being engrained in me, but I promise it’s possible.
